   150→+		return errors.New("invalid update options: checkpoint ID is required")
   151→+	}
   152→+
   153→+	// Ensure sessions branch exists
   154→+	if err := s.ensureSessionsBranch(); err != nil {
   155→+		return fmt.Errorf("failed to ensure sessions branch: %w", err)
   156→+	}
   157→+
   158→+	// Get current branch tip and flatten tree
   159→+	ref, entries, err := s.getSessionsBranchEntries()
   160→+	if err != nil {
   161→+		return err
   162→+	}
   163→+
   164→+	// Read root CheckpointSummary to find the session slot
   165→+	basePath := opts.CheckpointID.Path() + "/"
   166→+	rootMetadataPath := basePath + paths.MetadataFileName
   167→+	entry, exists := entries[rootMetadataPath]
   168→+	if !exists {
   169→+		return ErrCheckpointNotFound
   170→+	}
   171→+
   172→+	checkpointSummary, err := s.readSummaryFromBlob(entry.Hash)
   173→+	if err != nil {
   174→+		return fmt.Errorf("failed to read checkpoint summary: %w", err)
   175→+	}
   176→+	if len(checkpointSummary.Sessions) == 0 {
   177→+		return ErrCheckpointNotFound
   178→+	}
   179→+
   180→+	// Find session index matching opts.SessionID
   181→+	sessionIndex := -1
   182→+	for i := range len(checkpointSummary.Sessions) {
   183→+		metaPath := fmt.Sprintf("%s%d/%s", basePath, i, paths.MetadataFileName)
   184→+		if metaEntry, metaExists := entries[metaPath]; metaExists {
   185→+			meta, metaErr := s.readMetadataFromBlob(metaEntry.Hash)
   186→+			if metaErr == nil && meta.SessionID == opts.SessionID {
   187→+				sessionIndex = i
   188→+				break
   189→+			}
   190→+		}
   191→+	}
   192→+	if sessionIndex == -1 {
   193→+		// Fall back to latest session; log so mismatches are diagnosable.
   194→+		sessionIndex = len(checkpointSummary.Sessions) - 1
   195→+		logging.Debug(ctx, "UpdateCommitted: session ID not found, falling back to latest",
   196→+			slog.String("session_id", opts.SessionID),
   197→+			slog.String("checkpoint_id", string(opts.CheckpointID)),
   198→+			slog.Int("fallback_index", sessionIndex),
   199→+		)
   200→+	}
   201→+
   202→+	sessionPath := fmt.Sprintf("%s%d/", basePath, sessionIndex)
   203→+
   204→+	// Replace transcript (full replace, not append)
   205→+	// Apply redaction as safety net (caller should redact, but we ensure it here)
   206→+	if len(opts.Transcript) > 0 {
   207→+		transcript, err := redact.JSONLBytes(opts.Transcript)
   208→+		if err != nil {
   209→+			return fmt.Errorf("failed to redact transcript secrets: %w", err)
   210→+		}
   211→+		if err := s.replaceTranscript(transcript, opts.Agent, sessionPath, entries); err != nil {
   212→+			return fmt.Errorf("failed to replace transcript: %w", err)
   213→+		}
   214→+	}
   215→+
   216→+	// Replace prompts (apply redaction as safety net)
   217→+	if len(opts.Prompts) > 0 {
   218→+		promptContent := redact.String(strings.Join(opts.Prompts, "\n\n---\n\n"))
   219→+		blobHash, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, []byte(promptContent))
   220→+		if err != nil {
   221→+			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create prompt blob: %w", err)
   222→+		}
   223→+		entries[sessionPath+paths.PromptFileName] = object.TreeEntry{
   224→+			Name: sessionPath + paths.PromptFileName,
   225→+			Mode: filemode.Regular,
   226→+			Hash: blobHash,
   227→+		}
   228→+	}
   229→+
   230→+	// Replace context (apply redaction as safety net)
   231→+	if len(opts.Context) > 0 {
   232→+		contextBlob, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, redact.Bytes(opts.Context))
   233→+		if err != nil {
   234→+			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create context blob: %w", err)
   235→+		}
   236→+		entries[sessionPath+paths.ContextFileName] = object.TreeEntry{
   237→+			Name: sessionPath + paths.ContextFileName,
   238→+			Mode: filemode.Regular,
   239→+			Hash: contextBlob,
   240→+		}
   241→+	}
   242→+
   243→+	// Build and commit
   244→+	newTreeHash, err := BuildTreeFromEntries(s.repo, entries)
   245→+	if err != nil {
   246→+		return err
   247→+	}
   248→+
   249→+	authorName, authorEmail := getGitAuthorFromRepo(s.repo)
   250→+	commitMsg := fmt.Sprintf("Finalize transcript for checkpoint %s", opts.CheckpointID)
   251→+	newCommitHash, err := s.createCommit(newTreeHash, ref.Hash(), commitMsg, authorName, authorEmail)
   252→+	if err != nil {
   253→+		return err
   254→+	}
   255→+
   256→+	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
   257→+	newRef := plumbing.NewHashReference(refName, newCommitHash)
   258→+	if err := s.repo.Storer.SetReference(newRef); err != nil {
   259→+		return fmt.Errorf("failed to set branch reference: %w", err)
   260→+	}
   261→+
   262→+	return nil
   263→+}

   265→+// replaceTranscript writes the full transcript content, replacing any existing transcript.
   266→+// Also removes any chunk files from a previous write and updates the content hash.
   267→+func (s *GitStore) replaceTranscript(transcript []byte, agentType agent.AgentType, sessionPath string, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) error {
   268→+	// Remove existing transcript files (base + any chunks)
   269→+	transcriptBase := sessionPath + paths.TranscriptFileName
   270→+	for key := range entries {
   271→+		if key == transcriptBase || strings.HasPrefix(key, transcriptBase+".") {
   272→+			delete(entries, key)
   273→+		}
   274→+	}
   275→+
   276→+	// Chunk the transcript (matches writeTranscript behavior)
   277→+	chunks, err := agent.ChunkTranscript(transcript, agentType)
   278→+	if err != nil {
   279→+		return fmt.Errorf("failed to chunk transcript: %w", err)
   280→+	}
   281→+
   282→+	// Write chunk files
   283→+	for i, chunk := range chunks {
   284→+		chunkPath := sessionPath + agent.ChunkFileName(paths.TranscriptFileName, i)
   285→+		blobHash, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, chunk)
   286→+		if err != nil {
   287→+			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create transcript blob: %w", err)
   288→+		}
   289→+		entries[chunkPath] = object.TreeEntry{
   290→+			Name: chunkPath,
   291→+			Mode: filemode.Regular,
   292→+			Hash: blobHash,
   293→+		}
   294→+	}
   295→+
   296→+	// Update content hash
   297→+	contentHash := fmt.Sprintf("sha256:%x", sha256.Sum256(transcript))
   298→+	hashBlob, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, []byte(contentHash))
   299→+	if err != nil {
   300→+		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create content hash blob: %w", err)
   301→+	}
   302→+	hashPath := sessionPath + paths.ContentHashFileName
   303→+	entries[hashPath] = object.TreeEntry{
   304→+		Name: hashPath,
   305→+		Mode: filemode.Regular,
   306→+		Hash: hashBlob,
   307→+	}
   308→+
   309→+	return nil
   310→+}

   967→+func (r *ClaudeCodeRunner) RunPromptWithTools(ctx context.Context, workDir string, prompt string, tools []string) (*AgentResult, error) {
   968→+	// Build command: claude --model <model> -p "<prompt>" --allowedTools <tools>
   969→+	args := []string{
   970→+		"--model", r.Model,
   971→+		"-p", prompt,
   972→+	}
   973→+
   974→+	if len(tools) > 0 {
   975→+		// Claude CLI expects each tool as a separate argument after --allowedTools
   976→+		// e.g., --allowedTools Edit Read Bash (not --allowedTools "Edit,Read,Bash")
   977→+		args = append(args, "--allowedTools")
   978→+		args = append(args, tools...)
   979→+	}
   980→+
   981→+	// Create context with timeout
   982→+	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, r.Timeout)
   983→+	defer cancel()
   984→+
   985→+	//nolint:gosec // args are constructed from trusted config, not user input
   986→+	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "claude", args...)
   987→+	cmd.Dir = workDir
   988→+
   989→+	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
   990→+	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
   991→+	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
   992→+
   993→+	start := time.Now()
   994→+	err := cmd.Run()
   995→+	duration := time.Since(start)
   996→+
   997→+	result := &AgentResult{
   998→+		Stdout:   stdout.String(),
   999→+		Stderr:   stderr.String(),
  1000→+		Duration: duration,
  1001→+	}
  1002→+
  1003→+	if err != nil {
  1004→+		exitErr := &exec.ExitError{}
  1005→+		if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
  1006→+			result.ExitCode = exitErr.ExitCode()
  1007→+		} else {
  1008→+			result.ExitCode = -1
  1009→+		}
  1010→+		//nolint:wrapcheck // error is from exec.Run, caller can check ExitCode in result
  1011→+		return result, err
  1012→+	}
  1013→+
  1014→+	result.ExitCode = 0
  1015→+	return result, nil
  1016→+}

  2440→+// All tests share this binary to avoid repeated builds.

  2443→+// defaultAgent holds the agent to test with, determined in TestMain.
  2444→+var defaultAgent string
  2445→+
  2446→+// TestMain builds the CLI binary once and checks agent availability before running tests.
  2447→+func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
  2448→+	// Determine which agent to test with
  2449→+	defaultAgent = os.Getenv("E2E_AGENT")
  2450→+	if defaultAgent == "" {
  2451→+		defaultAgent = AgentNameClaudeCode
  2452→+	}
  2453→+
  2454→+	// Check if the agent is available
  2455→+	runner := NewAgentRunner(defaultAgent, AgentRunnerConfig{})
  2456→+	available, err := runner.IsAvailable()
  2457→+	if !available {
  2458→+		fmt.Printf("Agent %s not available (%v), skipping E2E tests\n", defaultAgent, err)
  2459→+		// Exit 0 to not fail CI when agent isn't configured
  2460→+		os.Exit(0)
  2461→+	}
  2462→+
  2463→+	// Build binary once to a temp directory
  2464→+	tmpDir, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "entire-e2e-test-*")
  2465→+	if err != nil {
  2466→+		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "failed to create temp dir for binary: %v\n", err)
  2467→+		os.Exit(1)
  2468→+	}
  2469→+
  2470→+	testBinaryPath = filepath.Join(tmpDir, "entire")
  2471→+
  2472→+	moduleRoot := findModuleRoot()
  2473→+	ctx := context.Background()
  2474→+
  2475→+	buildCmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "go", "build", "-o", testBinaryPath, ".")
  2476→+	buildCmd.Dir = filepath.Join(moduleRoot, "cmd", "entire")
  2477→+
  2478→+	buildOutput, err := buildCmd.CombinedOutput()
  2479→+	if err != nil {
  2480→+		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "failed to build CLI binary: %v\nOutput: %s\n", err, buildOutput)
  2481→+		os.RemoveAll(tmpDir)
  2482→+		os.Exit(1)
  2483→+	}
  2484→+
  2485→+	// Add binary to PATH so hooks can find it.
  2486→+	// This is safe because:
  2487→+	// 1. TestMain runs once before any tests (no parallel conflict with os.Setenv)
  2488→+	// 2. Each test package gets its own TestMain execution
  2489→+	// 3. PATH is restored in the same TestMain after m.Run() completes
  2490→+	// 4. The binary path is unique per test run (temp dir)
  2491→+	origPath := os.Getenv("PATH")
  2492→+	os.Setenv("PATH", tmpDir+string(os.PathListSeparator)+origPath)
  2493→+
  2494→+	// Run tests
  2495→+	code := m.Run()
  2496→+
  2497→+	// Cleanup
  2498→+	os.Setenv("PATH", origPath)
  2499→+	os.RemoveAll(tmpDir)
  2500→+	os.Exit(code)
  2501→+}

  2503→+// getTestBinary returns the path to the shared test binary.

  2512→+// findModuleRoot finds the Go module root by walking up from the current file.
  2513→+func findModuleRoot() string {
  2514→+	_, thisFile, _, ok := runtime.Caller(0)
  2515→+	if !ok {
  2516→+		panic("failed to get current file path via runtime.Caller")
  2517→+	}
  2518→+	dir := filepath.Dir(thisFile)
  2519→+
  2520→+	for {
  2521→+		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "go.mod")); err == nil {
  2522→+			return dir
  2523→+		}
  2524→+		parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
  2525→+		if parent == dir {
  2526→+			panic("could not find go.mod starting from " + thisFile)
  2527→+		}
  2528→+		dir = parent
  2529→+	}
  2530→+}

  2980→+// GetLatestCheckpointIDFromHistory walks backwards from HEAD and returns
  2981→+// the checkpoint ID from the first commit with an Entire-Checkpoint trailer.
  2982→+// Returns an error if no checkpoint trailer is found in any commit.
  2983→+func (env *TestEnv) GetLatestCheckpointIDFromHistory() (string, error) {
  2984→+	env.T.Helper()
  2985→+
  2986→+	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
  2987→+	if err != nil {
  2988→+		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
  2989→+	}
  2990→+
  2991→+	head, err := repo.Head()
  2992→+	if err != nil {
  2993→+		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get HEAD: %v", err)
  2994→+	}
  2995→+
  2996→+	commitIter, err := repo.Log(&git.LogOptions{From: head.Hash()})
  2997→+	if err != nil {
  2998→+		env.T.Fatalf("failed to iterate commits: %v", err)
  2999→+	}
  3000→+
  3001→+	var checkpointID string
  3002→+	//nolint:errcheck,gosec // ForEach callback returns error to stop iteration, not a real error
  3003→+	commitIter.ForEach(func(c *object.Commit) error {
  3004→+		// Look for Entire-Checkpoint trailer
  3005→+		for _, line := range strings.Split(c.Message, "\n") {
  3006→+			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
  3007→+			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "Entire-Checkpoint:") {
  3008→+				checkpointID = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "Entire-Checkpoint:"))
  3009→+				return errors.New("stop iteration")
  3010→+			}
  3011→+		}
  3012→+		return nil
  3013→+	})
  3014→+
  3015→+	if checkpointID == "" {
  3016→+		return "", errors.New("no commit with Entire-Checkpoint trailer found in history")
  3017→+	}
  3018→+
  3019→+	return checkpointID, nil
  3020→+}

  3263→+// TestShadow_DeferredTranscriptFinalization tests that HandleTurnEnd updates
  3264→+// the provisional transcript (written at commit time) with the full transcript
  3265→+// (available at turn end).
  3266→+//
  3267→+// Flow:
  3268→+// 1. Agent starts working (ACTIVE)
  3269→+// 2. Agent makes file changes
  3270→+// 3. User commits while agent is ACTIVE → provisional transcript condensed
  3271→+// 4. Agent continues work (updates transcript)
  3272→+// 5. Agent finishes (SimulateStop) → transcript finalized via UpdateCommitted
  3273→+//
  3274→+// This verifies that the final transcript on entire/checkpoints/v1 includes
  3275→+// work done AFTER the commit.

  3288→+	state, err := env.GetSessionState(sess.ID)

  3296→+	// Create file and initial transcript
  3297→+	env.WriteFile("feature.go", "package main\n\nfunc Feature() {}\n")
  3298→+	sess.CreateTranscript("Create feature function", []FileChange{
  3299→+		{Path: "feature.go", Content: "package main\n\nfunc Feature() {}\n"},
  3300→+	})
  3301→+
  3302→+	// Debug: verify session state before commit

  3304→+	if preCommitState == nil {
  3305→+		t.Fatal("Session state should exist before commit")

  3307→+	t.Logf("Pre-commit session state: phase=%s, worktreePath=%s, baseCommit=%s",
  3308→+		preCommitState.Phase, preCommitState.WorktreePath, preCommitState.BaseCommit[:7])
  3309→+
  3310→+	// User commits while agent is still ACTIVE

  3322→+		prepCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir

  3383→+	t.Logf("Provisional transcript length: %d bytes", len(provisionalContent))
  3384→+
  3385→+	// Verify session state has TurnCheckpointIDs for deferred finalization

  3398→+	sess.TranscriptBuilder.AddToolResult(toolID)

  3424→+			"Provisional: %d bytes\nFinalized: %d bytes",

  3429→+	if !strings.Contains(finalContent, "Also add a helper function") {

  3436→+	// Verify session is now IDLE

  3626→+// TestShadow_MultipleCommits_SameActiveTurn tests that multiple commits
  3627→+// during a single ACTIVE turn each get unique checkpoint IDs, and all
  3628→+// are finalized when the turn ends.
  3629→+//
  3630→+// Flow:
  3631→+// 1. Agent starts working (ACTIVE)
  3632→+// 2. User commits file A → checkpoint #1 (provisional)
  3633→+// 3. User commits file B → checkpoint #2 (provisional)
  3634→+// 4. User commits file C → checkpoint #3 (provisional)
  3635→+// 5. Agent finishes (SimulateStop) → all 3 checkpoints finalized

  3637→+	t.Parallel()
  3638→+
  3639→+	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, strategy.StrategyNameManualCommit)
  3640→+

  3648→+	// Create multiple files

  3651→+	env.WriteFile("fileC.go", "package main\n\nfunc C() {}\n")

  3656→+		{Path: "fileC.go", Content: "package main\n\nfunc C() {}\n"},
  3657→+	})
  3658→+
  3659→+	// Commit each file separately while ACTIVE
  3660→+	checkpointIDs := make([]string, 3)
  3661→+
  3662→+	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add file A", "fileA.go")
  3663→+	checkpointIDs[0] = env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(env.GetHeadHash())
  3664→+	if checkpointIDs[0] == "" {
  3665→+		t.Fatal("First commit should have checkpoint trailer")
  3666→+	}
  3667→+
  3668→+	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add file B", "fileB.go")
  3669→+	checkpointIDs[1] = env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(env.GetHeadHash())
  3670→+	if checkpointIDs[1] == "" {
  3671→+		t.Fatal("Second commit should have checkpoint trailer")
  3672→+	}
  3673→+
  3674→+	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add file C", "fileC.go")
  3675→+	checkpointIDs[2] = env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(env.GetHeadHash())
  3676→+	if checkpointIDs[2] == "" {
  3677→+		t.Fatal("Third commit should have checkpoint trailer")
  3678→+	}
  3679→+
  3680→+	t.Logf("Checkpoint IDs: %v", checkpointIDs)
  3681→+
  3682→+	// All checkpoint IDs must be unique
  3683→+	seen := make(map[string]bool)
  3684→+	for i, cpID := range checkpointIDs {
  3685→+		if seen[cpID] {
  3686→+			t.Errorf("Duplicate checkpoint ID at position %d: %s", i, cpID)
  3687→+		}
  3688→+		seen[cpID] = true
  3689→+	}
  3690→+
  3691→+	// Verify TurnCheckpointIDs contains all 3
  3692→+	state, err := env.GetSessionState(sess.ID)
  3693→+	if err != nil {
  3694→+		t.Fatalf("GetSessionState failed: %v", err)
  3695→+	}
  3696→+	if len(state.TurnCheckpointIDs) != 3 {
  3697→+		t.Errorf("TurnCheckpointIDs should have 3 entries, got %d: %v",
  3698→+			len(state.TurnCheckpointIDs), state.TurnCheckpointIDs)
  3699→+	}
  3700→+
  3701→+	// Add more work to transcript before stopping
  3702→+	sess.TranscriptBuilder.AddAssistantMessage("All files created successfully!")

  3704→+		t.Fatalf("Failed to write transcript: %v", err)
  3705→+	}
  3706→+
  3707→+	// Agent finishes - this should finalize ALL checkpoints
  3708→+	if err := env.SimulateStop(sess.ID, sess.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
  3709→+		t.Fatalf("SimulateStop failed: %v", err)
  3710→+	}
  3711→+
  3712→+	// Verify session is IDLE
  3713→+	state, err = env.GetSessionState(sess.ID)
  3714→+	if err != nil {

  3716→+	}
  3717→+	if state.Phase != session.PhaseIdle {
  3718→+		t.Errorf("Expected IDLE phase, got %s", state.Phase)
  3719→+	}
  3720→+
  3721→+	// TurnCheckpointIDs should be cleared after finalization
  3722→+	if len(state.TurnCheckpointIDs) != 0 {
  3723→+		t.Errorf("TurnCheckpointIDs should be cleared, got %v", state.TurnCheckpointIDs)
  3724→+	}
  3725→+
  3726→+	// Verify all checkpoints exist and have finalized transcripts
  3727→+	for i, cpID := range checkpointIDs {
  3728→+		transcriptPath := SessionFilePath(cpID, paths.TranscriptFileName)
  3729→+		content, found := env.ReadFileFromBranch(paths.MetadataBranchName, transcriptPath)
  3730→+		if !found {

  3733→+		}

  3737→+		}
  3738→+	}

  3743→+// TestShadow_OverlapCheck_UnrelatedCommit tests that commits for files NOT

  3774→+

  5031→+// Content-aware overlap detection for checkpoint management.
  5032→+//
  5033→+// These functions determine whether a commit contains session-related work by comparing
  5034→+// file content (not just filenames) against the shadow branch. This enables accurate
  5035→+// detection of the "reverted and replaced" scenario where a user:
  5036→+// 1. Reverts session changes (e.g., git checkout -- file.txt)
  5037→+// 2. Creates completely different content in the same file
  5038→+// 3. Commits the new content
  5039→+//
  5040→+// In this scenario, the commit should NOT get a checkpoint trailer because the
  5041→+// session's work was discarded, not incorporated.
  5042→+//
  5043→+// The key distinction:
  5044→+// - Modified files (exist in parent commit): Always count as overlap, regardless of
  5045→+//   content changes. The user is editing session's work.
  5046→+// - New files (don't exist in parent): Require content match against shadow branch.
  5047→+//   If content differs completely, the session's work was likely reverted & replaced.
  5048→+
  5049→+// filesOverlapWithContent checks if any file in filesTouched overlaps with the committed
  5050→+// content, using content-aware comparison to detect the "reverted and replaced" scenario.
  5051→+//
  5052→+// This is used in PostCommit to determine if a session has work in the commit.
  5053→+func filesOverlapWithContent(repo *git.Repository, shadowBranchName string, headCommit *object.Commit, filesTouched []string) bool {
  5054→+	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
  5055→+
  5056→+	// Build set of filesTouched for quick lookup
  5057→+	touchedSet := make(map[string]bool)
  5058→+	for _, f := range filesTouched {
  5059→+		touchedSet[f] = true
  5060→+	}
  5061→+
  5062→+	// Get HEAD commit tree (the committed content)
  5063→+	headTree, err := headCommit.Tree()
  5064→+	if err != nil {
  5065→+		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: failed to get HEAD tree, falling back to filename check",
  5066→+			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  5067→+		)
  5068→+		return len(filesTouched) > 0 // Fall back: assume overlap if any files touched
  5069→+	}
  5070→+
  5071→+	// Get shadow branch tree (the session's content)
  5072→+	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
  5073→+	shadowRef, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
  5074→+	if err != nil {
  5075→+		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: shadow branch not found, falling back to filename check",
  5076→+			slog.String("branch", shadowBranchName),
  5077→+			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  5078→+		)
  5079→+		return len(filesTouched) > 0 // Fall back: assume overlap if any files touched
  5080→+	}
  5081→+
  5082→+	shadowCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(shadowRef.Hash())
  5083→+	if err != nil {
  5084→+		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: failed to get shadow commit, falling back to filename check",
  5085→+			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  5086→+		)
  5087→+		return len(filesTouched) > 0
  5088→+	}
  5089→+
  5090→+	shadowTree, err := shadowCommit.Tree()
  5091→+	if err != nil {
  5092→+		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: failed to get shadow tree, falling back to filename check",
  5093→+			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  5094→+		)
  5095→+		return len(filesTouched) > 0
  5096→+	}
  5097→+
  5098→+	// Get the parent commit tree to determine if files are modified vs newly created.
  5099→+	// For modified files (exist in parent), we count as overlap regardless of content
  5100→+	// because the user is editing the session's work.
  5101→+	// For newly created files (don't exist in parent), we check content to detect
  5102→+	// the "reverted and replaced" scenario where user deleted session's work and
  5103→+	// created something completely different.
  5104→+	var parentTree *object.Tree
  5105→+	if headCommit.NumParents() > 0 {
  5106→+		if parent, err := headCommit.Parent(0); err == nil {
  5107→+			if pTree, err := parent.Tree(); err == nil {
  5108→+				parentTree = pTree
  5109→+			}
  5110→+		}
  5111→+	}
  5112→+
  5113→+	// Check each file in filesTouched
  5114→+	for _, filePath := range filesTouched {
  5115→+		// Get file from HEAD tree
  5116→+		headFile, err := headTree.File(filePath)
  5117→+		if err != nil {
  5118→+			// File not in HEAD commit - doesn't count as overlap
  5119→+			continue
  5120→+		}
  5121→+
  5122→+		// Check if this is a modified file (exists in parent) or new file
  5123→+		isModified := false
  5124→+		if parentTree != nil {
  5125→+			if _, err := parentTree.File(filePath); err == nil {
  5126→+				isModified = true
  5127→+			}
  5128→+		}

  5130→+		// Modified files always count as overlap (user edited session's work)
  5131→+		if isModified {
  5132→+			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: modified file counts as overlap",
  5133→+				slog.String("file", filePath),
  5134→+			)
  5135→+			return true
  5136→+		}
  5137→+
  5138→+		// For new files, check content against shadow branch
  5139→+		shadowFile, err := shadowTree.File(filePath)
  5140→+		if err != nil {
  5141→+			// File not in shadow branch - this shouldn't happen but skip it
  5142→+			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: file in filesTouched but not in shadow branch",
  5143→+				slog.String("file", filePath),
  5144→+			)
  5145→+			continue
  5146→+		}
  5147→+
  5148→+		// Compare by hash (blob hash) - exact content match required for new files
  5149→+		if headFile.Hash == shadowFile.Hash {
  5150→+			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: new file content match found",
  5151→+				slog.String("file", filePath),
  5152→+				slog.String("hash", headFile.Hash.String()),
  5153→+			)
  5154→+			return true
  5155→+		}
  5156→+
  5157→+		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: new file content mismatch (may be reverted & replaced)",
  5158→+			slog.String("file", filePath),
  5159→+			slog.String("head_hash", headFile.Hash.String()),
  5160→+			slog.String("shadow_hash", shadowFile.Hash.String()),
  5161→+		)
  5162→+	}
  5163→+
  5164→+	logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: no overlapping files found",
  5165→+		slog.Int("files_checked", len(filesTouched)),
  5166→+	)
  5167→+	return false
  5168→+}

  5170→+// stagedFilesOverlapWithContent checks if any staged file overlaps with filesTouched,

  5172→+//
  5173→+// For modified files (already exist in HEAD), we count as overlap because the user

  5176→+//

  5223→+	}

  5225→+	// Check each staged file
  5226→+	for _, stagedPath := range stagedFiles {
  5227→+		if !touchedSet[stagedPath] {
  5228→+			continue // Not in filesTouched, skip
  5229→+		}
  5230→+
  5231→+		// Check if this is a modified file (exists in HEAD) or new file
  5232→+		_, headErr := headTree.File(stagedPath)
  5233→+		isModified := headErr == nil
  5234→+
  5235→+		// Modified files always count as overlap (user edited session's work)
  5236→+		if isModified {
  5237→+			logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: modified file counts as overlap",
  5238→+				slog.String("file", stagedPath),
  5239→+			)
  5240→+			return true
  5241→+		}
  5242→+
  5243→+		// For new files, check content against shadow branch
  5244→+		stagedHash, found := indexEntries[stagedPath]
  5245→+		if !found {
  5246→+			continue // Not in index (shouldn't happen but be safe)
  5247→+		}
  5248→+
  5249→+		// Get file from shadow branch tree
  5250→+		shadowFile, err := shadowTree.File(stagedPath)
  5251→+		if err != nil {
  5252→+			// File not in shadow branch - doesn't count as content match

  5254→+				slog.String("file", stagedPath),
  5255→+			)
  5256→+			continue
  5257→+		}
  5258→+

  5260→+		if stagedHash == shadowFile.Hash {
  5261→+			logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: new file content match found",
  5262→+				slog.String("file", stagedPath),
  5263→+				slog.String("hash", stagedHash.String()),
  5264→+			)
  5265→+			return true
  5266→+		}
  5267→+
  5268→+		logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: new file content mismatch (may be reverted & replaced)",

  5270→+			slog.String("staged_hash", stagedHash.String()),
  5271→+			slog.String("shadow_hash", shadowFile.Hash.String()),
  5272→+		)
  5273→+	}

  5276→+		slog.Int("staged_files", len(stagedFiles)),
  5277→+		slog.Int("files_touched", len(filesTouched)),

  5284→+func hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, filesTouched []string) bool {

  5286→+	for _, f := range filesTouched {

  5300→+//
  5301→+// A file has remaining agent changes if:

  5340→+		)

  5342→+	}
  5343→+

  5345→+	if err != nil {
  5346→+		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: failed to get shadow tree, falling back to file subtraction",
  5347→+			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  5348→+		)

  5357→+			remaining = append(remaining, filePath)

  5359→+				slog.String("file", filePath),

  5368→+			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: file not in shadow branch, skipping",
  5369→+				slog.String("file", filePath),
  5370→+			)
  5371→+			continue
  5372→+		}
  5373→+
  5374→+		commitFile, err := commitTree.File(filePath)
  5375→+		if err != nil {
  5376→+			// File not in commit tree (deleted?) - keep it if it's in shadow
  5377→+			remaining = append(remaining, filePath)
  5378→+			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: file not in commit tree but in shadow, keeping",
  5379→+				slog.String("file", filePath),
  5380→+			)
  5381→+			continue
  5382→+		}

  5386→+			remaining = append(remaining, filePath)
  5387→+			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: content mismatch, keeping for carry-forward",

  5389→+				slog.String("commit_hash", commitFile.Hash.String()[:7]),
  5390→+				slog.String("shadow_hash", shadowFile.Hash.String()[:7]),
  5391→+			)
  5392→+		} else {
  5393→+			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: content fully committed",
  5394→+				slog.String("file", filePath),
  5395→+			)
  5396→+		}
  5397→+	}
  5398→+
  5399→+	logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: result",
  5400→+		slog.Int("files_touched", len(filesTouched)),
  5401→+		slog.Int("committed_files", len(committedFiles)),
  5402→+		slog.Int("remaining_files", len(remaining)),
  5403→+	)
  5404→+
  5405→+	return remaining
  5406→+}

  5408→+// subtractFilesByName returns files from filesTouched that are NOT in committedFiles.

  5410→+func subtractFilesByName(filesTouched []string, committedFiles map[string]struct{}) []string {
  5411→+	var remaining []string
  5412→+	for _, f := range filesTouched {
  5413→+		if _, committed := committedFiles[f]; !committed {
  5414→+			remaining = append(remaining, f)
  5415→+		}
  5416→+	}
  5417→+	return remaining

   632→	sess.CreateTranscript("Create files A, B, and C", []FileChange{
   633→		{Path: "fileA.go", Content: "package main\n\nfunc A() {}\n"},
   634→		{Path: "fileB.go", Content: "package main\n\nfunc B() {}\n"},
   635→		{Path: "fileC.go", Content: "package main\n\nfunc C() {}\n"},
   636→	})
   637→
   638→	// Stop session (becomes IDLE)
   639→	if err := env.SimulateStop(sess.ID, sess.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
   640→		t.Fatalf("SimulateStop failed: %v", err)
   641→	}
   642→
   643→	// First commit: files A and B
   644→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add files A and B", "fileA.go", "fileB.go")
   645→	firstCommitHash := env.GetHeadHash()
   646→	firstCheckpointID := env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(firstCommitHash)
   647→	if firstCheckpointID == "" {
   648→		t.Fatal("First commit should have checkpoint trailer (files overlap with session)")
   649→	}
   650→	t.Logf("First checkpoint ID: %s", firstCheckpointID)
   651→
   652→	// Second commit: file C
   653→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add file C", "fileC.go")
   654→	secondCommitHash := env.GetHeadHash()
   655→	secondCheckpointID := env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(secondCommitHash)
   656→	// Note: Whether this gets a checkpoint depends on carry-forward implementation
   657→	// for IDLE sessions. Log either way.
   658→	if secondCheckpointID != "" {
   659→		t.Logf("Second checkpoint ID: %s (carry-forward active for IDLE)", secondCheckpointID)
   660→	} else {
   661→		t.Log("Second commit has no checkpoint (IDLE sessions don't carry forward)")
   662→	}
   663→
   664→	// Verify session state - FilesTouched should be empty or session ended
   665→	state, err := env.GetSessionState(sess.ID)
   666→	if err != nil {
   667→		// Session may have been cleaned up, which is fine
   668→		t.Logf("Session state not found (may have been cleaned up): %v", err)
   669→	} else {

   671→			state.Phase, state.FilesTouched)
   672→	}
   673→
   674→	// Now manually edit file A (which was already committed as part of session)
   675→	env.WriteFile("fileA.go", "package main\n\n// Manual edit by user\nfunc A() { return }\n")
   676→
   677→	// Commit the manual edit - should NOT get checkpoint
   678→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Manual edit to file A", "fileA.go")
   679→	thirdCommitHash := env.GetHeadHash()
   680→	thirdCheckpointID := env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(thirdCommitHash)
   681→
   682→	if thirdCheckpointID != "" {
   683→		t.Errorf("Third commit should NOT have checkpoint trailer "+
   684→			"(manual edit after session depleted), got %s", thirdCheckpointID)
   685→	} else {

   687→	}
   688→
   689→	t.Log("SessionDepleted_ManualEditNoCheckpoint test completed successfully")
   690→}
   691→
   692→// TestShadow_RevertedFiles_ManualEditNoCheckpoint tests that after reverting
   693→// uncommitted session files, manual edits with completely different content
   694→// do NOT get checkpoint trailers.
   695→//
   696→// The overlap check is content-aware: it compares file hashes between the
   697→// committed content and the shadow branch content. If they don't match,
   698→// the file is not considered session-related.
   699→//
   700→// Flow:
   701→// 1. Agent creates files A, B, C, then stops (IDLE)
   702→// 2. User commits files A and B → checkpoint #1
   703→// 3. User reverts file C (deletes it)
   704→// 4. User manually creates file C with different content
   705→// 5. User commits file C → NO checkpoint (content doesn't match shadow branch)
   706→func TestShadow_RevertedFiles_ManualEditNoCheckpoint(t *testing.T) {
   707→	t.Parallel()
   708→
   709→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, strategy.StrategyNameManualCommit)
   710→
   711→	sess := env.NewSession()
   712→
   713→	// Start session
   714→	if err := env.SimulateUserPromptSubmit(sess.ID); err != nil {
   715→		t.Fatalf("SimulateUserPromptSubmit failed: %v", err)
   716→	}
   717→
   718→	// Create 3 files through session
   719→	env.WriteFile("fileA.go", "package main\n\nfunc A() {}\n")
   720→	env.WriteFile("fileB.go", "package main\n\nfunc B() {}\n")
   721→	env.WriteFile("fileC.go", "package main\n\nfunc C() {}\n")
   722→	sess.CreateTranscript("Create files A, B, and C", []FileChange{
   723→		{Path: "fileA.go", Content: "package main\n\nfunc A() {}\n"},
   724→		{Path: "fileB.go", Content: "package main\n\nfunc B() {}\n"},
   725→		{Path: "fileC.go", Content: "package main\n\nfunc C() {}\n"},
   726→	})
   727→
   728→	// Stop session (becomes IDLE)
   729→	if err := env.SimulateStop(sess.ID, sess.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
   730→		t.Fatalf("SimulateStop failed: %v", err)
   731→	}
   732→
   733→	// First commit: files A and B
   734→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add files A and B", "fileA.go", "fileB.go")
   735→	firstCommitHash := env.GetHeadHash()
   736→	firstCheckpointID := env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(firstCommitHash)
   737→	if firstCheckpointID == "" {
   738→		t.Fatal("First commit should have checkpoint trailer (files overlap with session)")
   739→	}
   740→	t.Logf("First checkpoint ID: %s", firstCheckpointID)
   741→
   742→	// Revert file C (undo agent's changes)
   743→	// Since fileC.go is a new file (untracked), we need to delete it
   744→	if err := os.Remove(filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, "fileC.go")); err != nil {
   745→		t.Fatalf("Failed to remove fileC.go: %v", err)
   746→	}
   747→	t.Log("Reverted fileC.go by removing it")
   748→
   749→	// Verify file C is gone
   750→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, "fileC.go")); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
   751→		t.Fatal("fileC.go should not exist after revert")
   752→	}
   753→
   754→	// User manually creates file C with DIFFERENT content (not what agent wrote)
   755→	env.WriteFile("fileC.go", "package main\n\n// Completely different implementation\nfunc C() { panic(\"manual\") }\n")
   756→
   757→	// Commit the manual file C - should NOT get checkpoint because content-aware
   758→	// overlap check compares file hashes. The content is completely different
   759→	// from what the session wrote, so it's not linked.
   760→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add file C (manual implementation)", "fileC.go")
   761→	secondCommitHash := env.GetHeadHash()
   762→	secondCheckpointID := env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(secondCommitHash)
   763→
   764→	if secondCheckpointID != "" {
   765→		t.Errorf("Second commit should NOT have checkpoint trailer "+
   766→			"(content doesn't match shadow branch), got %s", secondCheckpointID)
   767→	} else {
   768→		t.Log("Second commit correctly has no checkpoint trailer (content mismatch)")
   769→	}
   770→
   771→	t.Log("RevertedFiles_ManualEditNoCheckpoint test completed successfully")
   772→}

1→# Checkpoint Scenarios 2→ 3→This document describes how the one-to-one checkpoint system handles various user workflows. 4→ 5→## Overview 6→ 7→The system uses: 8→- **Shadow branches** (`entire/-`) - temporary storage for checkpoint data 9→- **FilesTouched** - accumulates files modified during the session 10→- **1:1 checkpoints** - each commit gets its own unique checkpoint ID 11→- **Content-aware overlap** - prevents linking commits where user reverted session changes 12→ 13→## State Machine 14→ 15→```mermaid 16→stateDiagram-v2 17→ [*] --> IDLE : SessionStart 18→ 19→ IDLE --> ACTIVE : TurnStart (UserPromptSubmit) 20→ ACTIVE --> IDLE : TurnEnd (Stop hook) 21→ ACTIVE --> ACTIVE : GitCommit / Condense 22→ IDLE --> IDLE : GitCommit / Condense 23→ 24→ IDLE --> ENDED : SessionStop 25→ ACTIVE --> ENDED : SessionStop 26→ ENDED --> ACTIVE : TurnStart (session resume) 27→ ENDED --> ENDED : GitCommit / CondenseIfFilesTouched 28→``` 29→ 30→--- 31→ 32→## Scenario 1: Prompt → Changes → Prompt Finishes → User Commits 33→ 34→The simplest workflow: user runs a prompt, Claude makes changes, prompt finishes, then user manually commits. 35→ 36→```mermaid 37→sequenceDiagram 38→ participant U as User 39→ participant C as Claude 40→ participant G as Git Hooks 41→ participant S as Session State 42→ participant SB as Shadow Branch 43→ 44→ U->>C: Submit prompt 45→ Note over G: UserPromptSubmit hook 46→ G->>S: InitializeSession (IDLE→ACTIVE) 47→ S->>S: TurnID generated 48→ 49→ C->>C: Makes changes (A, B, C) 50→ C->>G: SaveChanges (Stop hook) 51→ G->>SB: Write checkpoint (A, B, C + transcript) 52→ G->>S: FilesTouched = [A, B, C] 53→ Note over G: TurnEnd: ACTIVE→IDLE 54→ 55→ Note over U: Later... 56→ U->>G: git commit -a 57→ Note over G: PrepareCommitMsg hook 58→ G->>S: Check FilesTouched [A, B, C] 59→ G->>G: staged [A,B,C] ∩ FilesTouched → overlap ✓ 60→ G->>G: Generate checkpoint ID, add trailer 61→ 62→ Note over G: PostCommit hook 63→ G->>G: EventGitCommit (IDLE) 64→ G->>SB: Condense to entire/checkpoints/v1 65→ G->>SB: Delete shadow branch 66→ G->>S: FilesTouched = nil 67→``` 68→ 69→### Key Points 70→- Shadow branch holds checkpoint data until user commits 71→- PrepareCommitMsg adds `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer 72→- PostCommit condenses to permanent storage and cleans up 73→ 74→--- 75→ 76→## Scenario 2: Prompt Commits Within Single Turn 77→ 78→Claude is instructed to commit changes, so the commit happens during the ACTIVE phase. 79→ 80→```mermaid 81→sequenceDiagram 82→ participant U as User 83→ participant C as Claude 84→ participant G as Git Hooks 85→ participant S as Session State 86→ participant SB as Shadow Branch 87→ 88→ U->>C: "Make changes and commit them" 89→ Note over G: UserPromptSubmit hook 90→ G->>S: InitializeSession (→ACTIVE) 91→ 92→ C->>C: Makes changes (A, B) 93→ C->>G: git add && git commit 94→ 95→ Note over G: PrepareCommitMsg (no TTY = agent commit) 96→ G->>G: Generate checkpoint ID, add trailer directly 97→ 98→ Note over G: PostCommit hook (ACTIVE) 99→ G->>G: EventGitCommit (ACTIVE→ACTIVE) 100→ G->>SB: Condense with provisional transcript 101→ G->>S: TurnCheckpointIDs += [checkpoint-id] 102→ G->>S: FilesTouched = nil 103→ 104→ C->>G: Responds with summary 105→ Note over G: Stop hook 106→ G->>G: HandleTurnEnd (ACTIVE→IDLE) 107→ G->>G: UpdateCommitted: finalize with full transcript 108→ G->>S: TurnCheckpointIDs = nil 109→``` 110→ 111→### Key Points 112→- Agent commits detected by no TTY → fast path adds trailer directly 113→- **Deferred finalization**: PostCommit saves provisional transcript, HandleTurnEnd updates with full transcript 114→- TurnCheckpointIDs tracks mid-turn checkpoints for finalization at stop 115→ 116→--- 117→ 118→## Scenario 3: Claude Makes Multiple Granular Commits 119→ 120→Claude is instructed to make granular commits, resulting in multiple commits during one turn. 121→ 122→```mermaid 123→sequenceDiagram 124→ participant U as User 125→ participant C as Claude 126→ participant G as Git Hooks 127→ participant S as Session State 128→ 129→ U->>C: "Implement feature with granular commits" 130→ Note over G: UserPromptSubmit → ACTIVE 131→ 132→ C->>C: Creates file A 133→ C->>G: git commit -m "Add A" 134→ Note over G: PrepareCommitMsg: checkpoint-1 135→ Note over G: PostCommit (ACTIVE) 136→ G->>G: Condense checkpoint-1 (provisional) 137→ G->>S: TurnCheckpointIDs = [checkpoint-1] 138→ 139→ C->>C: Creates file B 140→ C->>G: git commit -m "Add B" 141→ Note over G: PrepareCommitMsg: checkpoint-2 142→ Note over G: PostCommit (ACTIVE) 143→ G->>G: Condense checkpoint-2 (provisional) 144→ G->>S: TurnCheckpointIDs = [checkpoint-1, checkpoint-2] 145→ 146→ C->>C: Creates file C 147→ C->>G: git commit -m "Add C" 148→ Note over G: PrepareCommitMsg: checkpoint-3 149→ Note over G: PostCommit (ACTIVE) 150→ G->>G: Condense checkpoint-3 (provisional) 151→ G->>S: TurnCheckpointIDs = [checkpoint-1, checkpoint-2, checkpoint-3] 152→ 153→ C->>G: Summary response 154→ Note over G: Stop hook → HandleTurnEnd 155→ G->>G: Finalize ALL checkpoints with full transcript 156→ Note right of G: checkpoint-1: UpdateCommitted
checkpoint-2: UpdateCommitted
checkpoint-3: UpdateCommitted 157→ G->>S: TurnCheckpointIDs = nil 158→``` 159→ 160→### Key Points 161→- Each commit gets its own unique checkpoint ID (1:1 model) 162→- All checkpoints are finalized together at turn end 163→- Each checkpoint has the full session transcript for context 164→ 165→--- 166→ 167→## Scenario 4: User Splits Changes Into Multiple Commits 168→ 169→User decides to create multiple commits from Claude's changes after the prompt finishes. 170→ 171→```mermaid 172→sequenceDiagram 173→ participant U as User 174→ participant C as Claude 175→ participant G as Git Hooks 176→ participant S as Session State 177→ participant SB as Shadow Branch 178→ 179→ U->>C: Submit prompt 180→ Note over G: UserPromptSubmit → ACTIVE 181→ 182→ C->>C: Makes changes (A, B, C, D) 183→ C->>G: SaveChanges (Stop hook) 184→ G->>SB: Write checkpoint (A, B, C, D) 185→ G->>S: FilesTouched = [A, B, C, D] 186→ Note over G: TurnEnd: ACTIVE→IDLE 187→ 188→ Note over U: User commits A, B only 189→ U->>G: git add A B && git commit 190→ Note over G: PrepareCommitMsg: checkpoint-1 191→ Note over G: PostCommit (IDLE) 192→ G->>G: committedFiles = {A, B} 193→ G->>G: remaining = [C, D] 194→ G->>SB: Condense checkpoint-1 195→ G->>SB: Carry-forward C, D to new shadow branch 196→ G->>S: FilesTouched = [C, D] 197→ 198→ Note over U: User commits C, D 199→ U->>G: git add C D && git commit 200→ Note over G: PrepareCommitMsg: checkpoint-2 201→ Note over G: PostCommit (IDLE) 202→ G->>G: committedFiles = {C, D} 203→ G->>G: remaining = [] 204→ G->>SB: Condense checkpoint-2 205→ G->>S: FilesTouched = nil 206→``` 207→ 208→### Key Points 209→- **Carry-forward logic**: uncommitted files get a new shadow branch 210→- Each commit gets its own checkpoint ID (1:1 model) 211→- Both checkpoints link to the same session transcript 212→ 213→### Content-Aware Carry-Forward 214→ 215→The carry-forward logic uses **content-aware comparison** to determine which files have remaining uncommitted changes: 216→ 217→1. **File not in commit** → definitely has remaining changes 218→2. **File in commit, hash matches shadow branch** → fully committed, no carry-forward 219→3. **File in commit, hash differs from shadow branch** → partial commit (e.g., `git add -p`), carry forward 220→ 221→This enables splitting changes within a single file across multiple commits (see Scenario 7). 222→ 223→--- 224→ 225→## Scenario 5: Partial Commit → Stash → Next Prompt 226→ 227→User commits some changes, stashes the rest, then runs another prompt. 228→ 229→```mermaid 230→sequenceDiagram 231→ participant U as User 232→ participant C as Claude 233→ participant G as Git Hooks 234→ participant S as Session State 235→ participant SB as Shadow Branch 236→ 237→ U->>C: Prompt 1 238→ Note over G: UserPromptSubmit → ACTIVE 239→ 240→ C->>C: Makes changes (A, B, C) 241→ C->>G: Stop hook 242→ G->>SB: Checkpoint (A, B, C) 243→ G->>S: FilesTouched = [A, B, C] 244→ Note over G: ACTIVE→IDLE 245→ 246→ Note over U: User commits A only 247→ U->>G: git add A && git commit 248→ Note over G: PostCommit 249→ G->>SB: Condense checkpoint-1 250→ G->>SB: Carry-forward B, C 251→ G->>S: FilesTouched = [B, C] 252→ 253→ Note over U: User stashes B, C 254→ U->>U: git stash 255→ Note right of U: B, C removed from working directory
FilesTouched still = [B, C] 256→ 257→ U->>C: Prompt 2 258→ Note over G: UserPromptSubmit (IDLE→ACTIVE) 259→ G->>S: TurnID = new, TurnCheckpointIDs = nil 260→ Note right of G: FilesTouched NOT cleared
(accumulates across prompts) 261→ 262→ C->>C: Makes changes (D, E) 263→ C->>G: SaveChanges 264→ G->>SB: Add D, E to shadow branch tree 265→ Note right of SB: Tree now has: B, C (old) + D, E (new) 266→ G->>S: FilesTouched = merge([B,C], [D,E]) = [B,C,D,E] 267→ Note over G: ACTIVE→IDLE 268→ 269→ Note over U: User commits D, E 270→ U->>G: git add D E && git commit 271→ Note over G: PrepareCommitMsg 272→ G->>G: staged [D,E] ∩ FilesTouched [B,C,D,E] → D,E match ✓ 273→ G->>G: checkpoint-2 trailer added 274→ 275→ Note over G: PostCommit 276→ G->>G: committedFiles = {D, E} 277→ G->>G: remaining = [B, C] 278→ G->>SB: Condense checkpoint-2 279→ Note right of G: Checkpoint has FULL session transcript
(both Prompt 1 and Prompt 2) 280→ 281→ G->>G: Carry-forward attempt for B, C 282→ Note right of G: B, C don't exist on disk (stashed)
→ removed from tree 283→ G->>S: FilesTouched = [B, C] 284→``` 285→ 286→### Key Points 287→- **FilesTouched accumulates** across prompts (not cleared at TurnStart) 288→- **Checkpoints have full session context**: D, E commit links to transcript showing BOTH prompts 289→- **No wrong attribution**: Looking at checkpoint-2, you can see D, E were created by Prompt 2 290→ 291→### Edge Case: Stashed Files Lose Shadow Content 292→ 293→After user commits D, E, the carry-forward for B, C creates an "empty" checkpoint: 294→- `buildTreeWithChanges` removes non-existent files (B, C are stashed) from the tree 295→- A shadow branch commit is created, but its tree is just HEAD (no B, C content) 296→- `FilesTouched` is set to `[B, C]` - the files are still **tracked by name** 297→ 298→**If user later unstashes B, C and commits them:** 299→- PrepareCommitMsg: staged [B, C] overlaps with FilesTouched [B, C] by filename → trailer added ✓ 300→- PostCommit: checkpoint is created and linked 301→- But the shadow branch doesn't have the original B, C content from Prompt 1 302→ 303→This is acceptable behavior - stashing files mid-session and committing other files first is an explicit user action. The files are still tracked, but the shadow branch content chain is broken. 304→ 305→--- 306→ 307→## Scenario 6: Stash → Second Prompt → Unstash → Commit All 308→ 309→User stashes files, runs another prompt, then unstashes and commits everything together. 310→ 311→```mermaid 312→sequenceDiagram 313→ participant U as User 314→ participant C as Claude 315→ participant G as Git Hooks 316→ participant S as Session State 317→ participant SB as Shadow Branch 318→ 319→ U->>C: Prompt 1 320→ Note over G: UserPromptSubmit → ACTIVE 321→ 322→ C->>C: Makes changes (A, B, C) 323→ C->>G: Stop hook 324→ G->>SB: Checkpoint (A, B, C) 325→ G->>S: FilesTouched = [A, B, C] 326→ Note over G: ACTIVE→IDLE 327→ 328→ Note over U: User commits A only 329→ U->>G: git add A && git commit 330→ Note over G: PostCommit 331→ G->>SB: Condense checkpoint-1 332→ G->>SB: Carry-forward B, C 333→ G->>S: FilesTouched = [B, C] 334→ 335→ Note over U: User stashes B, C 336→ U->>U: git stash 337→ Note right of U: B, C removed from working directory
Shadow branch still has B, C 338→ 339→ U->>C: Prompt 2 340→ Note over G: UserPromptSubmit (IDLE→ACTIVE) 341→ 342→ C->>C: Makes changes (D, E) 343→ C->>G: Stop hook (SaveChanges) 344→ G->>SB: Add D, E to existing shadow branch 345→ Note right of SB: Tree: B, C (from base) + D, E (new) 346→ G->>S: FilesTouched = merge([B,C], [D,E]) = [B,C,D,E] 347→ Note over G: ACTIVE→IDLE 348→ 349→ Note over U: User unstashes B, C 350→ U->>U: git stash pop 351→ Note right of U: B, C back in working directory 352→ 353→ Note over U: User commits ALL files 354→ U->>G: git add B C D E && git commit 355→ Note over G: PrepareCommitMsg 356→ G->>G: staged [B,C,D,E] ∩ FilesTouched [B,C,D,E] → all match ✓ 357→ G->>G: checkpoint-2 trailer added 358→ 359→ Note over G: PostCommit 360→ G->>G: committedFiles = {B, C, D, E} 361→ G->>G: remaining = [] 362→ G->>SB: Condense checkpoint-2 363→ Note right of G: Checkpoint includes ALL files (B,C,D,E)
and FULL transcript (both prompts) 364→ G->>S: FilesTouched = nil 365→``` 366→ 367→### Key Points 368→- **Shadow branch accumulates**: D, E added on top of existing B, C from carry-forward 369→- **All files tracked**: When user commits all together, all four files link to checkpoint 370→- **Full session context**: Checkpoint transcript shows Prompt 1 created B, C and Prompt 2 created D, E 371→ 372→### Contrast with Scenario 5 373→ 374→| Scenario | User Action | Result | 375→|----------|-------------|--------| 376→| **5**: Commit D, E first, then B, C later | Commits D, E while B, C stashed | B, C "fall out" - carry-forward fails, later commit of B, C has no shadow content | 377→| **6**: Commit all together after unstash | Unstashes B, C, commits B, C, D, E together | All files linked to single checkpoint | 378→ 379→The key difference is **when the commit happens relative to the unstash**: 380→- If you commit while files are stashed → those files lose their shadow branch content 381→- If you unstash first, then commit → all files are preserved together 382→ 383→--- 384→ 385→## Scenario 7: Partial Staging with `git add -p` 386→ 387→User uses interactive staging to commit only some hunks of a file, leaving other agent changes uncommitted. 388→ 389→```mermaid 390→sequenceDiagram 391→ participant U as User 392→ participant C as Claude 393→ participant G as Git Hooks 394→ participant S as Session State 395→ participant SB as Shadow Branch 396→ 397→ U->>C: Submit prompt 398→ Note over G: UserPromptSubmit → ACTIVE 399→ 400→ C->>C: Makes multiple changes to file A 401→ Note right of C: A now has lines 1-100
(was empty before) 402→ C->>G: Stop hook 403→ G->>SB: Checkpoint (A with lines 1-100) 404→ G->>S: FilesTouched = [A] 405→ Note over G: ACTIVE→IDLE 406→ 407→ Note over U: User stages partial content 408→ U->>G: git add -p A 409→ Note right of U: Stages only lines 1-50
Worktree still has 1-100 410→ 411→ U->>G: git commit 412→ Note over G: PrepareCommitMsg: checkpoint-1 413→ 414→ Note over G: PostCommit 415→ G->>G: committedFiles = {A} 416→ G->>G: Content check: committed A (lines 1-50) 417→ G->>G: Shadow A hash ≠ committed A hash 418→ G->>G: remaining = [A] (has uncommitted changes) 419→ G->>SB: Condense checkpoint-1 420→ G->>SB: Carry-forward A to new shadow branch 421→ Note right of SB: New shadow has A with
current worktree (lines 1-100) 422→ G->>S: FilesTouched = [A] 423→ 424→ Note over U: User commits remaining 425→ U->>G: git add A && git commit 426→ Note over G: PrepareCommitMsg: checkpoint-2 427→ 428→ Note over G: PostCommit 429→ G->>G: Content check: committed A == shadow A 430→ G->>G: remaining = [] 431→ G->>SB: Condense checkpoint-2 432→ G->>S: FilesTouched = nil 433→``` 434→ 435→### Key Points 436→- **Content-aware carry-forward**: Compares git blob hashes, not just filenames 437→- Partial staging (`git add -p`) within a single file is detected 438→- Each commit gets proper attribution, even when splitting one file's changes 439→ 440→### How Content Comparison Works 441→ 442→```mermaid 443→flowchart TD 444→ A[PostCommit: Carry-forward check] --> B{File in committedFiles?} 445→ B -->|No| C[✓ Add to remaining
File not committed at all] 446→ B -->|Yes| D[Get shadow branch file hash] 447→ D --> E{Shadow file exists?} 448→ E -->|No| F[Skip file
Nothing to compare against] 449→ E -->|Yes| G{Committed hash == shadow hash?} 450→ G -->|Yes| H[Skip file
Fully committed] 451→ G -->|No| I[✓ Add to remaining
Partial commit detected] 452→ 453→ C --> J[Carry forward remaining files] 454→ I --> J 455→``` 456→ 457→--- 458→ 459→## Content-Aware Overlap Detection 460→ 461→Prevents linking commits where user reverted session changes and wrote different content. 462→ 463→```mermaid 464→flowchart TD 465→ A[PostCommit: Check files overlap] --> B{File in commit AND in FilesTouched?} 466→ B -->|No| Z[No checkpoint trailer] 467→ B -->|Yes| C{File existed in parent commit?} 468→ C -->|Yes: Modified file| D[✓ Counts as overlap
User edited session's work] 469→ C -->|No: New file| E{Content hash matches shadow branch?} 470→ E -->|Yes| F[✓ Counts as overlap
Session's content preserved] 471→ E -->|No| G[✗ No overlap
User reverted & replaced] 472→ 473→ D --> H[Add checkpoint trailer] 474→ F --> H 475→ G --> Z 476→``` 477→ 478→### Example: Reverted and Replaced 479→ 480→```mermaid 481→sequenceDiagram 482→ participant U as User 483→ participant C as Claude 484→ participant G as Git Hooks 485→ 486→ C->>C: Creates file X with content "hello" 487→ Note over G: Shadow branch: X (hash: abc123) 488→ 489→ U->>U: Reverts: git checkout -- X 490→ U->>U: Writes completely different content 491→ Note right of U: X now has content "world"
(hash: def456) 492→ 493→ U->>G: git add X && git commit 494→ Note over G: PrepareCommitMsg 495→ G->>G: X in FilesTouched? Yes 496→ G->>G: X is new file (not in parent) 497→ G->>G: Compare hashes: abc123 ≠ def456 498→ G->>G: Content mismatch → NO overlap 499→ Note over G: No Entire-Checkpoint trailer added 500→``` 501→ 502→--- 503→ 504→## Summary Table 505→ 506→| Scenario | When Checkpoint Created | Checkpoint Contains | Key Mechanism | 507→|----------|------------------------|---------------------|---------------| 508→| 1. User commits after prompt | PostCommit (IDLE) | Full transcript | Normal condensation | 509→| 2. Claude commits in turn | PostCommit (ACTIVE) + HandleTurnEnd | Full transcript (finalized at stop) | Deferred finalization | 510→| 3. Multiple Claude commits | Each PostCommit (ACTIVE) + HandleTurnEnd | Full transcript per checkpoint | TurnCheckpointIDs tracking | 511→| 4. User splits commits | Each PostCommit (IDLE) | Full transcript per checkpoint | Content-aware carry-forward | 512→| 5. Partial commit + stash + new prompt + commit new | PostCommit (IDLE) | Full transcript (both prompts) | FilesTouched accumulation, stashed files "fall out" | 513→| 6. Stash + new prompt + unstash + commit all | PostCommit (IDLE) | All files + full transcript | Shadow branch accumulation | 514→| 7. Partial staging with `git add -p` | Each PostCommit (IDLE) | Full transcript per checkpoint | Content-aware carry-forward (hash comparison) | 515→ 516→--- 517→ 518→## Known Caveats 519→ 520→### 1. Redundant Transcript Data Across Commits 521→ 522→Each checkpoint stores the **full session transcript** up to that point. If a session results in multiple commits (Scenarios 3, 4, 5, 6), each checkpoint contains overlapping transcript data. 523→ 524→**Example**: Session with 3 commits 525→- Checkpoint 1: transcript lines 1-100 526→- Checkpoint 2: transcript lines 1-200 (includes 1-100 again) 527→- Checkpoint 3: transcript lines 1-300 (includes 1-200 again) 528→ 529→**Trade-off**: This simplifies checkpoint retrieval (each is self-contained) at the cost of storage efficiency. 530→ 531→### 2. Token Usage Sums Are Misleading 532→ 533→Each checkpoint's `metadata.json` contains cumulative token usage for the entire session up to that point. Summing token counts across multiple checkpoints from the same session **double-counts tokens**. 534→ 535→**Example**: 536→- Checkpoint 1: 10,000 tokens (session total so far) 537→- Checkpoint 2: 25,000 tokens (session total so far) 538→- Naive sum: 35,000 tokens ❌ 539→- Actual usage: 25,000 tokens ✓ 540→ 541→**Correct approach**: Use the token count from the **last checkpoint** of a session, or track incremental deltas separately. 542→ 543→### 3. Stashed Files Lose Shadow Content 544→ 545→As described in Scenario 5, if files are stashed and other files are committed first, the stashed files lose their content in the shadow branch. They remain tracked by filename in `FilesTouched`, but subsequent checkpoints won't have the original file content preserved. 546→ 547→### 4. No Per-File Prompt Attribution 548→ 549→Checkpoints don't explicitly tag which prompt created which file. To determine this, you must parse the transcript and correlate `tool_use` entries with preceding `user` messages. The `files_touched` list in metadata is cumulative across all prompts. 550→ 551→### 5. Carry-Forward Checkpoints Include Full Transcript 552→ 553→When files are carried forward (Scenario 4), `CheckpointTranscriptStart` is reset to 0. This means each carry-forward checkpoint includes the **entire transcript**, not just new content since the last checkpoint. 554→ 555→**Impact**: For long sessions with many partial commits, checkpoint storage grows linearly with session length × number of commits. 556→ 557→### 6. Crash Before HandleTurnEnd Leaves Provisional Transcripts 558→ 559→In Scenarios 2 and 3 (Claude commits during turn), checkpoints are saved with "provisional" transcripts during PostCommit. The full transcript is written at HandleTurnEnd (Stop hook). 560→ 561→If the session crashes or is killed before the Stop hook fires: 562→- Checkpoints exist with partial transcripts 563→- `TurnCheckpointIDs` in session state tracks which need finalization 564→- Next session start does **not** automatically finalize orphaned checkpoints 565→ 566→### 7. Two Different Content-Aware Checks 567→ 568→The system uses two separate content-aware checks with different purposes: 569→ 570→**A. Overlap Detection** (`filesOverlapWithContent`) - Determines if commit should be linked to session: 571→- Only applies to **newly created files** 572→- Modified files (existed in parent) **always count as overlap** 573→- Used in PrepareCommitMsg/PostCommit for non-ACTIVE sessions 574→- **Purpose**: Prevent linking commits where user reverted session content 575→ 576→**B. Carry-Forward Detection** (`filesWithRemainingAgentChanges`) - Determines which files to carry forward: 577→- Applies to **all committed files** 578→- Compares committed content hash vs shadow branch hash 579→- Hash mismatch = partial commit, file carried forward 580→- **Purpose**: Enable splitting changes within a file across commits (Scenario 7) 581→ 582→### 8. Carry-Forward Content Superseded by New Prompts 583→ 584→When files are carried forward and then a new prompt modifies the same file: 585→- The shadow branch gets the **new** content (from the new prompt's SaveChanges) 586→- The carried-forward content is overwritten 587→- Subsequent commits compare against the **new prompt's content**, not the original carried-forward content 588→ 589→**Example**: 590→1. Prompt 1: Agent writes 100 lines to file A 591→2. User commits 50 lines via `git add -p` 592→3. Carry-forward: A (with 100 lines) goes to new shadow branch 593→4. Prompt 2: Agent adds 50 more lines to A (now 150 lines total in worktree) 594→5. SaveChanges: Shadow branch now has A with 150 lines 595→6. User commits: Comparison is against 150 lines, not original 100 lines 596→ 597→This is correct behavior - the shadow branch reflects the **current combined state** of the session's work. 598→ 599→### 9. Automatic Cleanup During Normal Operations 600→ 601→Most orphaned data is cleaned up automatically: 602→ 603→- **Shadow branches**: Deleted after condensation if no other sessions reference them 604→- **Session states**: Cleaned up during session listing when shadow branch no longer exists (and session is not ACTIVE, has no `LastCheckpointID`) 605→ 606→For anything that slips through, run `entire clean` manually: 607→ 608→```bash 609→entire clean # Preview orphaned items 610→entire clean --force # Delete orphaned items 611→``` 612→ Whenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. 1→package strategy
     2→
     3→import (
     4→	"context"
     5→	"log/slog"
     6→
     7→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
     8→	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v5"
     9→	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v5/plumbing"
    10→	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v5/plumbing/object"
    11→)
    12→
    13→// Content-aware overlap detection for checkpoint management.
    14→//
    15→// These functions determine whether a commit contains session-related work by comparing
    16→// file content (not just filenames) against the shadow branch. This enables accurate
    17→// detection of the "reverted and replaced" scenario where a user:
    18→// 1. Reverts session changes (e.g., git checkout -- file.txt)
    19→// 2. Creates completely different content in the same file
    20→// 3. Commits the new content
    21→//
    22→// In this scenario, the commit should NOT get a checkpoint trailer because the
    23→// session's work was discarded, not incorporated.
    24→//
    25→// The key distinction:
    26→// - Modified files (exist in parent commit): Always count as overlap, regardless of
    27→//   content changes. The user is editing session's work.
    28→// - New files (don't exist in parent): Require content match against shadow branch.
    29→//   If content differs completely, the session's work was likely reverted & replaced.
    30→
    31→// filesOverlapWithContent checks if any file in filesTouched overlaps with the committed
    32→// content, using content-aware comparison to detect the "reverted and replaced" scenario.
    33→//
    34→// This is used in PostCommit to determine if a session has work in the commit.
    35→func filesOverlapWithContent(repo *git.Repository, shadowBranchName string, headCommit *object.Commit, filesTouched []string) bool {
    36→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
    37→
    38→	// Build set of filesTouched for quick lookup
    39→	touchedSet := make(map[string]bool)
    40→	for _, f := range filesTouched {
    41→		touchedSet[f] = true
    42→	}
    43→
    44→	// Get HEAD commit tree (the committed content)
    45→	headTree, err := headCommit.Tree()
    46→	if err != nil {
    47→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: failed to get HEAD tree, falling back to filename check",
    48→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
    49→		)
    50→		return len(filesTouched) > 0 // Fall back: assume overlap if any files touched
    51→	}
    52→
    53→	// Get shadow branch tree (the session's content)
    54→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
    55→	shadowRef, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
    56→	if err != nil {
    57→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: shadow branch not found, falling back to filename check",
    58→			slog.String("branch", shadowBranchName),
    59→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
    60→		)
    61→		return len(filesTouched) > 0 // Fall back: assume overlap if any files touched
    62→	}
    63→
    64→	shadowCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(shadowRef.Hash())
    65→	if err != nil {
    66→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: failed to get shadow commit, falling back to filename check",
    67→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
    68→		)
    69→		return len(filesTouched) > 0
    70→	}
    71→
    72→	shadowTree, err := shadowCommit.Tree()
    73→	if err != nil {
    74→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: failed to get shadow tree, falling back to filename check",
    75→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
    76→		)
    77→		return len(filesTouched) > 0
    78→	}
    79→
    80→	// Get the parent commit tree to determine if files are modified vs newly created.
    81→	// For modified files (exist in parent), we count as overlap regardless of content
    82→	// because the user is editing the session's work.
    83→	// For newly created files (don't exist in parent), we check content to detect
    84→	// the "reverted and replaced" scenario where user deleted session's work and
    85→	// created something completely different.
    86→	var parentTree *object.Tree
    87→	if headCommit.NumParents() > 0 {
    88→		if parent, err := headCommit.Parent(0); err == nil {
    89→			if pTree, err := parent.Tree(); err == nil {
    90→				parentTree = pTree
    91→			}
    92→		}
    93→	}
    94→
    95→	// Check each file in filesTouched
    96→	for _, filePath := range filesTouched {
    97→		// Get file from HEAD tree
    98→		headFile, err := headTree.File(filePath)
    99→		if err != nil {
   100→			// File not in HEAD commit - doesn't count as overlap
   101→			continue
   102→		}
   103→
   104→		// Check if this is a modified file (exists in parent) or new file
   105→		isModified := false
   106→		if parentTree != nil {
   107→			if _, err := parentTree.File(filePath); err == nil {
   108→				isModified = true
   109→			}
   110→		}
   111→
   112→		// Modified files always count as overlap (user edited session's work)
   113→		if isModified {
   114→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: modified file counts as overlap",
   115→				slog.String("file", filePath),
   116→			)
   117→			return true
   118→		}
   119→
   120→		// For new files, check content against shadow branch
   121→		shadowFile, err := shadowTree.File(filePath)
   122→		if err != nil {
   123→			// File not in shadow branch - this shouldn't happen but skip it
   124→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: file in filesTouched but not in shadow branch",
   125→				slog.String("file", filePath),
   126→			)
   127→			continue
   128→		}
   129→
   130→		// Compare by hash (blob hash) - exact content match required for new files
   131→		if headFile.Hash == shadowFile.Hash {
   132→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: new file content match found",
   133→				slog.String("file", filePath),
   134→				slog.String("hash", headFile.Hash.String()),
   135→			)
   136→			return true
   137→		}
   138→
   139→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: new file content mismatch (may be reverted & replaced)",
   140→			slog.String("file", filePath),
   141→			slog.String("head_hash", headFile.Hash.String()),
   142→			slog.String("shadow_hash", shadowFile.Hash.String()),
   143→		)
   144→	}
   145→
   146→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: no overlapping files found",
   147→		slog.Int("files_checked", len(filesTouched)),
   148→	)
   149→	return false
   150→}
   151→
   152→// stagedFilesOverlapWithContent checks if any staged file overlaps with filesTouched,
   153→// distinguishing between modified files (always overlap) and new files (check content).
   154→//
   155→// For modified files (already exist in HEAD), we count as overlap because the user
   156→// is editing the session's work. For new files (don't exist in HEAD), we require
   157→// content match to detect the "reverted and replaced" scenario.
   158→//
   159→// This is used in PrepareCommitMsg for carry-forward scenarios.
   160→func stagedFilesOverlapWithContent(repo *git.Repository, shadowTree *object.Tree, stagedFiles, filesTouched []string) bool {
   161→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   162→
   163→	// Build set of filesTouched for quick lookup
   164→	touchedSet := make(map[string]bool)
   165→	for _, f := range filesTouched {
   166→		touchedSet[f] = true
   167→	}
   168→
   169→	// Get HEAD tree to determine if files are being modified or newly created
   170→	head, err := repo.Head()
   171→	if err != nil {
   172→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: failed to get HEAD, falling back to filename check",
   173→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   174→		)
   175→		return hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, filesTouched)
   176→	}
   177→	headCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
   178→	if err != nil {
   179→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: failed to get HEAD commit, falling back to filename check",
   180→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   181→		)
   182→		return hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, filesTouched)
   183→	}
   184→	headTree, err := headCommit.Tree()
   185→	if err != nil {
   186→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: failed to get HEAD tree, falling back to filename check",
   187→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   188→		)
   189→		return hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, filesTouched)
   190→	}
   191→
   192→	// Get the git index to access staged file hashes
   193→	idx, err := repo.Storer.Index()
   194→	if err != nil {
   195→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: failed to get index, falling back to filename check",
   196→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   197→		)
   198→		return hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, filesTouched)
   199→	}
   200→
   201→	// Build a map of index entries for O(1) lookup (avoid O(n*m) nested loop)
   202→	indexEntries := make(map[string]plumbing.Hash, len(idx.Entries))
   203→	for _, entry := range idx.Entries {
   204→		indexEntries[entry.Name] = entry.Hash
   205→	}
   206→
   207→	// Check each staged file
   208→	for _, stagedPath := range stagedFiles {
   209→		if !touchedSet[stagedPath] {
   210→			continue // Not in filesTouched, skip
   211→		}
   212→
   213→		// Check if this is a modified file (exists in HEAD) or new file
   214→		_, headErr := headTree.File(stagedPath)
   215→		isModified := headErr == nil
   216→
   217→		// Modified files always count as overlap (user edited session's work)
   218→		if isModified {
   219→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: modified file counts as overlap",
   220→				slog.String("file", stagedPath),
   221→			)
   222→			return true
   223→		}
   224→
   225→		// For new files, check content against shadow branch
   226→		stagedHash, found := indexEntries[stagedPath]
   227→		if !found {
   228→			continue // Not in index (shouldn't happen but be safe)
   229→		}
   230→
   231→		// Get file from shadow branch tree
   232→		shadowFile, err := shadowTree.File(stagedPath)
   233→		if err != nil {
   234→			// File not in shadow branch - doesn't count as content match
   235→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: file not in shadow tree",
   236→				slog.String("file", stagedPath),
   237→			)
   238→			continue
   239→		}
   240→
   241→		// Compare hashes - for new files, require exact content match
   242→		if stagedHash == shadowFile.Hash {
   243→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: new file content match found",
   244→				slog.String("file", stagedPath),
   245→				slog.String("hash", stagedHash.String()),
   246→			)
   247→			return true
   248→		}
   249→
   250→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: new file content mismatch (may be reverted & replaced)",
   251→			slog.String("file", stagedPath),
   252→			slog.String("staged_hash", stagedHash.String()),
   253→			slog.String("shadow_hash", shadowFile.Hash.String()),
   254→		)
   255→	}
   256→
   257→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: no overlapping files found",
   258→		slog.Int("staged_files", len(stagedFiles)),
   259→		slog.Int("files_touched", len(filesTouched)),
   260→	)
   261→	return false
   262→}
   263→
   264→// hasOverlappingFiles checks if any file in stagedFiles appears in filesTouched.
   265→// This is a fallback when content-aware comparison isn't possible.
   266→func hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, filesTouched []string) bool {
   267→	touchedSet := make(map[string]bool)
   268→	for _, f := range filesTouched {
   269→		touchedSet[f] = true
   270→	}
   271→
   272→	for _, staged := range stagedFiles {
   273→		if touchedSet[staged] {
   274→			return true
   275→		}
   276→	}
   277→	return false
   278→}
   279→
   280→// filesWithRemainingAgentChanges returns files from filesTouched that still have
   281→// uncommitted agent changes. This is used for carry-forward after partial commits.
   282→//
   283→// A file has remaining agent changes if:
   284→//   - It wasn't committed at all (not in committedFiles), OR
   285→//   - It was committed but the committed content doesn't match the shadow branch
   286→//     (user committed partial changes, e.g., via git add -p)
   287→//
   288→// Falls back to file-level subtraction if shadow branch is unavailable.
   289→func filesWithRemainingAgentChanges(
   290→	repo *git.Repository,
   291→	shadowBranchName string,
   292→	headCommit *object.Commit,
   293→	filesTouched []string,
   294→	committedFiles map[string]struct{},
   295→) []string {
   296→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   297→
   298→	// Get HEAD commit tree (the committed content)
   299→	commitTree, err := headCommit.Tree()
   300→	if err != nil {
   301→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: failed to get commit tree, falling back to file subtraction",
   302→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   303→		)
   304→		return subtractFilesByName(filesTouched, committedFiles)
   305→	}
